sections.text: Construction costs fall into two main categories: hard costs (materials and labor directly related to building) and soft costs (permits, design, engineering, legal, financing). Hard costs typically represent 70-80% of total project cost. Soft costs take up the remaining 20-30%. Within hard costs, materials and labor are roughly equal at 50-50 for most projects, though material-heavy trades like concrete and steel may shift this ratio.

Construction costs vary significantly by region. The national average is the baseline, but costs in major cities can be 30-50% higher. Labor costs in high-cost-of-living areas, permitting fees, and material transportation costs all contribute. The construction cost estimator allows regional adjustment factors.

10-15% for new construction, 15-20% for renovations. Renovations have more unknowns (what is behind the walls), so the higher contingency is warranted. For major infrastructure or commercial projects, 5-10% is standard with a separate management reserve.
How do I account for material price fluctuations?

Include a 3-5% escalation factor for projects lasting more than 6 months. Lumber, steel, and fuel prices can fluctuate significantly. Getting fixed-price bids from suppliers within 30 days of ordering locks in current pricing.
